svg.title: Shoulder-save bobble
svg.text: The shoulder-save bobble (Genesis): why only the top net
To scale, with the game's own pictures (ghighl, frames 667 and 659). In a shoulder save the puck is held 14 up the screen from him.
The hold point is BEHIND him, past the net's
front. The puck is pulled there, the net
strips it off his stick, and it slides in
(the net never bounces a puck moving into it).
The hold point is in FRONT of him, out in
the ice. The puck stays on his stick, well
away from the net: nothing can happen.
It also needs him standing near his goal line and roughly centred when he catches it, which is why it's rare.
Recorded: one goal (ANA-ATL P3 4:00, a pass shot his stick popped up). Shoot high at the top net and follow it in.
